What is Tidewater?

Tidewater is a made-up storage engine used to test the podcast pipeline. It keeps every column of a table in its own file on disk. Teams use it to scan very large tables quickly. Tidewater is a made-up, high-performance storage engine used to test the podcast pipeline.

Why store columns separately?

A report usually reads a few columns out of many. Storing columns apart means the engine reads only the files it needs. This avoids loading unrelated data from disk. Row at a time As the diagram below shows, a row store reads whole rows instead.

Compression

Values in one column tend to look alike. Similar values compress very well. Smaller files mean less data moves between disk and memory. 
CREATE TABLE t (a INT) ENGINE = Tidewater;

Replication

Each table can be copied to several servers. If one server fails the others keep serving queries. Copies stay in step through a shared log.
